vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: sysadmin-toolbox
Version: 1.1.0

The skill is classified as suspicious due to its automated content refresh mechanism. The `SKILL.md` file explicitly instructs the AI agent to execute `scripts/refresh.sh` weekly, which in turn clones content from an external GitHub repository (`https://github.com/trimstray/the-book-of-secret-knowledge.git`) and overwrites local reference files. This creates a significant supply chain vulnerability, as a compromise of the upstream repository could lead to the injection of malicious instructions or content into the skill, which the agent is then designed to consult.

llm.summary: This skill is a broad sysadmin and security command reference, but it includes high-risk copy-paste commands and an unpinned refresh path that users should review carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: Several examples can affect production hosts, network services, disk devices, local credentials, or shared web roots, and the skill does not consistently require scoping, dry runs, backups, or explicit user confirmation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The included refresh script clones a mutable upstream GitHub branch and overwrites agent-consumed reference files; SKILL.md advertises weekly auto-refresh, although no scheduler was found in the package.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Auto-consult triggers are broad across routine troubleshooting, scripting, auditing, and pentesting, which can surface dangerous dual-use commands in ordinary administration contexts.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The references include commands that overwrite /etc/profile and install a future-session logout trap, and the refresh mechanism can persistently change future guidance after review.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated toolbox purpose fits many references, but the artifact also includes runnable remote shell, flood traffic, credential-capture, disk-wipe, global profile-modification, and unsafe permission examples without clear lab-only or authorization boundaries.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want a powerful sysadmin and security cheat sheet and are prepared to review commands before use. Disable or narrow auto-consult, avoid automatic refresh from mutable upstream content, and do not run examples that modify /etc, wipe disks, loosen permissions, capture credentials, flood networks, or expose shells except in owned, authorized, isolated environments.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: Downgraded: the referenced files are present and inspectable in this workspace, so the coverage claim did not by itself support escalation.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: the skill's automatic activation scope is broader than appropriate for references that include destructive and offensive operations.
[YR1] unexpected: Accepted in context: the netcat section contains copy-paste interactive shell exposure commands outside a clearly gated lab-only section.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: profile overwrites, disk wiping, plaintext credential capture, traffic flooding, and remote shell recipes are materially under-warned for broad auto-consult use.
[TM1] unexpected: Accepted: unsafe recursive permission examples are presented as generic commands without least-privilege framing or rollback guidance.
[PE3] expected: Mostly downgraded: examples involving /etc/passwd, SSH keys, known_hosts, and keychain are common administrative references and do not establish credential theft by themselves.
[E4] expected: Partially accepted: terminal recording is admin-relevant, but the artifact does not warn that logs may capture sensitive commands or output.
[YR4] expected: Tool references such as scanners and pentesting frameworks are expected for a security toolbox; the concern is the lack of scoping and the presence of runnable high-risk recipes.
[T04] unexpected: Accepted: unauthenticated interactive shell recipes create high-impact misuse risk when surfaced by a general toolbox skill.
[T06] unexpected: Accepted: the /etc/profile recipe creates persistent system-wide behavior and can terminate SSH-related processes without safeguards.
[T08] expected: Accepted as a control concern: refreshing from upstream is consistent with keeping references current, but doing so from an unpinned mutable branch directly into trusted references is under-controlled.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: broad chmod and delete examples are not proportionately guarded for routine operational use.
